items.title: Live: Trump says Iran 'could be taken out in one night' if Strait of Hormuz is not reopened
items.description: US President Donald Trump is holding a press conference with military officials at the White House to discuss the war in the Middle East. Follow live.

items.title: Iran briefing with Matthew Doran: Iran rejects truce deal
items.description: The clock is ticking down to US President Donald Trump's deadline, but Iran hasn't blinked.

items.title: Trump threatens 'demolition' of Iran and takes another swipe at Australia
items.description: Donald Trump says the "entire country" of Iran will be "taken out" if no deal is reached by Wednesday morning (AEST), ratcheting up his threat to target civilian infrastructure and brushing off concerns it would be a war crime.

items.title: They earn $350K but in this city they're 'left with nothing' each month
items.description: The US president and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani are from polar opposite ends of the political spectrum, but comic Ron Barba voted for them both.

items.title: Tech starts to eat itself as AI reshapes workforce
items.description: The wave of change from artificial intelligence rolling across the corporate landscape is going largely unnoticed as attention understandably shifts to an escalating war.

items.title: Live: Artemis II breaks distance record, Moon 'bright spot' named after commander's late wife
items.description: The Artemis II astronauts have travelled further from Earth than any humans before. The crew is now on a historic six-hour flyby of the Moon, capturing never-before-seen views of its far side. Follow live.

items.title: Fuel thieves targeting NSW truckers as they sleep
items.description: The owner of a trucking company in Western Sydney says most cases of fuel theft have occurred when his drivers have parked on the side of the road for the night.

items.title: Live: Energy expert says more drilling for oil won't fix fuel crisis
items.description: Energy expert Tony Wood is calling on the government to begin planning for Australia's next fuel crisis now — but says further oil exploration is not an immediate solution. Follow live.

items.title: Canberra woman in an aged care 'black hole' sees no way out
items.description: After being stuck in a hospital in Canberra for 19 months, paraplegic 84-year-old Mary Wansey has lost hope of ever finding a place in aged care.

items.title: Hospital apologises after man who needed urgent surgery was sent home
items.description: An Australian Navy candidate says he nearly lost his leg following delays in diagnosis and treatment of his emergency condition by two Perth hospitals.

items.title: Israeli settler violence in the West Bank deepens against backdrop of Iran war
items.description: Under the cover of regional conflict, Israelis who have established illegal settlements and outposts in the West Bank become emboldened to take over more land as world attention remains on the war in Iran.

items.title: Pro-climate son-in-law to Rupert Murdoch backs Farrer independent
items.description: Backers of Farrer independent candidate Michelle Milthorpe are celebrating after securing the support of a prominent pro-climate farmer who is also the son-in-law of media mogul Rupert Murdoch.

items.title: Live: ASX poised for higher open as Wall St rises
items.description: The Australian share market is set to open higher in morning trading. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: The first world country in the grip of a poverty crisis
items.description: London. It's the epicentre of Britain but without it the UK's GDP is equivalent to the poorest state in the US. And one fifth of the total population is living in poverty.

items.title: Zein speaks broken Arabic — here's how she made peace with that
items.description: For Heywire winner Zein, her family is remembered in the fragments she remembers of Syria.

items.title: Hidden costs mean many comedians make 'zero profit' from festival runs
items.description: Doing a run of shows at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival is the pinnacle for a lot of Australian comedians, but the festival's tens of thousands of punters are rarely privy to the behind-the-scenes costs.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Today's ABC Places quiz features photos from 10 locations around the world. Your challenge is to guess where you are.

items.title: How China uses ferries and fishing boats to pressure Taiwan
items.description: China has quietly mobilised thousands of fishing boats twice in recent months to form floating barriers at least 300 kilometres long.

items.title: 'Double whammy' for Ningaloo Reef amid fears cyclone wiped out coral spawning
items.description: As sharks swarm in the aftermath, there are fears Cyclone Narelle might be a climate disaster for the world-famous Ningaloo Reef.

items.title: A luxury beef giant's cattle died of thirst. Regulators were told later
items.description: The lack of investigation into deaths at the $700 million beef business has been described as "completely unacceptable" by a legal expert who argued industry had captured government regulators.

items.title: Tropical Cyclone Maila likely to cross Far North Queensland
items.description: The Bureau of Meteorology is increasingly confident the system will move towards the Queensland coast later in the week, potentially crossing Cape York Peninsula.

items.title: 'Are you sure?': First Nations voters asked about identity at polling booths
items.description: South Australia's Aboriginal Affairs Minister will consider an independent review of the state's Voice to Parliament election, following claims some voters were queried about their racial background at polling booths, while others were forced to queue for hours.

items.title: Owner of dog that mauled young girl charged over attack
items.description: The owner of a dog that mauled a young girl in the Perth suburb of Hillarys last month, leaving her with serious facial injuries, is charged under Western Australia's Dog Act.

items.title: 'No one else should go through this': Young job hunters a target in scam surge
items.description: Job seekers should be wary of sharing their bank account information with potential employers, as job scams targeting young people surge, according to Scamwatch.

items.title: Middle East war causes PVC prices to skyrocket
items.description: Conflict in the Middle East has disrupted petroleum and gas supply chains, causing PVC prices to skyrocket in Australia.
